# ScrollFrame

- Inherits [`UIObject`](uiobject.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("ScrollFrame")`

A `Frame` whose contents can be larger than it is (§2.2). It clips its descendants whatever `ClipsDescendants` says -- a scrolling region that did not clip would not be one.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AbsoluteCanvasSize` | `Vector2` | — | read-only | How large the canvas is, in pixels, as the last layout found it -- never smaller than the frame, and with `AutomaticCanvasSize` taken into account. |
| `AbsoluteWindowSize` | `Vector2` | — | read-only | How much of the canvas shows at once, in pixels, as the last layout found it: the frame's own size. `AbsoluteCanvasSize - AbsoluteWindowSize` is how far it can scroll. |
| `AutomaticCanvasSize` | `Enum.AutomaticSize` | `Enum.AutomaticSize.None` | read/write | Which axes the canvas grows along to hold its contents: a `UIListLayout`'s or a `UIGridLayout`'s line, or else the furthest any child reaches, with the frame's `UIPadding` around it. On such an axis the canvas is the larger of `CanvasSize` and the contents, so a list of rows added by a script scrolls without the script measuring them. |
| `CanvasPosition` | `Vector2` | `Vector2.zero` | read/write | How far the canvas is scrolled, in pixels. Clamped to what the canvas allows on the next layout, so a write past the end settles at the end rather than showing emptiness. |
| `CanvasSize` | `UDim2` | `UDim2.new()` | read/write | How big the scrollable area is. Children lay out against this rather than against the frame's own size. |
| `ElasticBehavior` | `Enum.ElasticBehavior` | `Enum.ElasticBehavior.WhenScrollable` | read/write | Whether a drag past the end gives -- less the further it goes -- and springs back when the finger lifts, and a fling that reaches the end bounces. `CanvasPosition` never leaves the canvas: the give is drawn, not reported. |
| `ScrollBarImageColor` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)` | read/write | The bar's colour: the thumb in it, and the track under the thumb in it at a quarter of the thumb's opacity. A middle grey by default, which reads on a light panel and on a dark one. |
| `ScrollBarImageTransparency` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How see-through the bar is, from 0 (solid) to 1 (gone, while the frame still scrolls). Apart from `BackgroundTransparency`: a clear list keeps its bar. |
| `ScrollBarThickness` | `number` | `12` | read/write | In pixels; zero draws no bar and still scrolls, which is what a touch surface wants.<br><br>A bar appears only on an axis that can actually move: a canvas that fits its region gets none, because a bar for an axis with nowhere to go is a bar that lies. The thumb is as long a fraction of the track as the view is of the canvas, and never shorter than the bar is wide -- a thumb of two pixels in a very long canvas is a thumb nobody can grab. **The thumb can be dragged**: the canvas follows it, as far along the canvas as the thumb is along its track.<br><br>The bar is drawn OUTSIDE the region's own clip, or it would scroll away with the content it reports on. |
| `ScrollingDirection` | `Enum.ScrollingDirection` | `Enum.ScrollingDirection.XY` | read/write | Which axes a hand scrolls along. **A drag in a frame inside another goes to the one that scrolls the way the drag started**: a vertical list on a horizontal carousel scrolls down when the finger goes down and lets the carousel have a sideways drag, and the axis is kept until the finger lifts. |
| `ScrollingEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether a hand can scroll it: the wheel, a drag, a fling, the bar and a selection moved out of view. A script's `CanvasPosition` writes still move it -- a list that scrolls itself to the newest line can still be one nobody else scrolls. |
